title: Check yourself: The tool builder: what the agent may write

questions.stem: A generated tool declares that it reads files, and its code fetches a web page. What does the gate in this module's practice do?

options.text: Approves it, since reading and fetching are both low-risk effects here
options.says: Ruled out because the difference is the finding: "the gate compares what the code does with what was declared and refuses the difference".

options.text: Refuses it, since the proposal never mentioned that effect
options.says: Code that does more than it declared is refused.

options.text: Sends it back for a better description, since the declaration was incomplete
options.says: Ruled out because the finding is a refusal and not a request for a better description: "Compare what the code does with the permissions declared, and refuse the difference".

options.text: Holds it for a person to approve, since a fetch is a risky effect
options.says: Ruled out because the network is denied by policy and not held for a person: "The third asks for the network, which the policy denies, so it is refused whatever its code says."

questions.stem: A team runs generated tools in a container that has no network access, no secrets and a short lifetime. A colleague says that the code scan is therefore unnecessary. What is the best reply?

options.text: It is a cheap first check for the obvious, and the surroundings hold back the rest
options.says: The scan is the cheap first check.

options.text: It is unnecessary only when the container is also given the secrets it needs to work
options.says: Ruled out because the container holds no secrets: "The lesson for a team that runs generated code itself is the same, and it is a list of absences: no network, no secrets, no shared state, a short life and limits on time and memory."

options.text: It is the real protection, and the container only adds some speed to each run
options.says: Ruled out because the scan finds only what its authors thought of: "A scan finds what its authors thought of: a call spelled differently, built from strings or imported by name slips past it."

options.text: It is unnecessary, and the container alone makes generated tools safe whatever their code does
options.says: Ruled out because the scan still does useful work: "The scan is useful for what it does well: it refuses the obvious".

origin.section: A text scan is not a sandbox

questions.stem: In the example, a tool that was approved by the reviewer returns a result without the field that its schema promised. What happens to the result?

options.text: It is passed to the agent with a warning attached to the front of it
options.says: Ruled out because a result that does not match is not passed on: "a result that does not match its schema is rejected before the agent sees it".

options.text: It is filled with a default and passed on to let the run continue
options.says: Ruled out because the check does not repair data: "Treat the result as data and check it against its schema".

options.text: It is refused before the agent ever sees it
options.says: A result is checked before the agent uses it.

options.text: It is rejected, and the reviewer's approval is withdrawn for every later tool in the run
options.says: Ruled out because the approval covers one proposal: "the approval covers the proposal that was reviewed and not a later version".
